name: Las Vegas
tagline: Neon desert spectacle of appetite, chance and showmanship.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, May, Jun, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: March-April and October-November bring desert comfort and a packed calendar of racing, rodeo and Sphere residencies; the brutal summer heat is best kept to the pool, and New Year turns the Strip into the world's largest party.

ourTake.lede: Vegas rewards a clear plan and a short stay, decide whether you're here for the tables, the restaurants and shows, or the desert beyond, because trying to do all three blurs into exhaustion. The genuine luxury is off the casino floor: a great meal, a residency show, and a day trip to red rock or the canyon. Two or three nights is plenty; the Strip loses its charm faster than most expect.
ourTake.comeIf: You want shows, dining and the Grand Canyon on a wider American trip.
ourTake.skipIf: You dislike crowds and casinos; the appeal is loud and unapologetic.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Wynn Las Vegas
items.description: Steve Wynn's copper-glass masterpiece, the largest Forbes Five-Star resort in the world, and it feels it.

items.name: Encore at Wynn Las Vegas
items.description: Wynn's warmer, red-and-gold sister tower, all-suite by design, and Forbes Five-Star in its own right.

items.name: ARIA Resort & Casino
credentials: The Spa & Salon at ARIA, Forbes 5-Star (2025)
items.description: The Strip's most modern grand hotel, a AAA Five Diamond resort of glass, art and quiet technology.

items.name: Bellagio
items.description: The lake, the fountains, the Chihuly ceiling, the hotel that taught Las Vegas to do elegance, still AAA Five Diamond.

items.name: The Venetian Resort Las Vegas
items.description: Grand Canal, frescoes and gondolas, an all-suite palazzo, and one of the largest luxury hotels in the world.

items.name: The Palazzo at The Venetian Resort
items.description: The Venetian's quieter, all-suite sibling, a calmer, greener wing of the same palazzo world.

items.name: Fontainebleau Las Vegas
items.description: The long-awaited blue tower at the north end, Miami's Fontainebleau reborn as the Strip's newest grand resort.

items.name: Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas
items.description: The Strip's serene non-gaming, non-smoking tower, a hushed Waldorf Astoria sky-lobby above the noise.

items.name: Four Seasons Hotel Las Vegas
credentials: The Spa at Four Seasons, Forbes 5-Star (2025)
items.description: The original non-gaming Strip oasis, Four Seasons calm on the top floors of Mandalay Bay, with its own private entrance.

items.name: Crockfords Las Vegas, LXR Hotels & Resorts
items.description: Hilton's ultra-luxury LXR flag inside Resorts World, the most rarefied of its three towers, with butler service.

items.name: Bellagio Fountains
items.description: The free choreographed water ballet on Lake Bellagio, jets soaring 460 feet, set to opera, Sinatra or Bollywood-adjacent classics, runs every 15-30 minutes into the night. Book a fountain-view suite or a Lakeside table so the family watches from a private balcony rather than the pavement crush.

items.name: Bellagio Conservatory & Botanical Gardens
items.description: A 14,000-square-foot glasshouse re-planted five times a year with towering seasonal displays, a hushed, fragrant, entirely free interlude off the casino floor. Genuinely all-ages and calm, a rare thing on the Strip, and a favourite photo stop for multi-generational groups.

items.name: Sphere, 'The Sphere Experience: Postcard from Earth'
items.description: Darren Aronofsky's 50-minute film plays across the world's largest wraparound 16K LED screen, with haptic seats, wind and scent, a hyper-real journey around the planet that leaves first-timers speechless. Splurge on the premium seating and let the concierge time your visit to also catch the Exosphere lit up outside.

items.name: The Sphere Exosphere
items.description: The 580,000-square-foot exterior, 1.2 million LED pucks turning the whole 366-foot orb into a giant eyeball, emoji, or spinning globe, is best seen for free from a Venetian balcony or a rooftop cocktail. A five-minute spectacle that has become the city's new skyline signature.

items.name: The Venetian & Grand Canal Shoppes, Gondola Rides
items.description: A singing gondolier poles you along an indoor canal beneath a painted sky, past St Mark's Square recreated in marble, kitsch executed at grand scale, and irresistible with children. Private gondolas can be reserved for couples or a family, away from the shared queue.

items.name: 'O' by Cirque du Soleil
items.description: Cirque's aquatic masterwork at the Bellagio, staged in, on and above a 1.5-million-gallon pool where synchronised swimmers, divers and aerialists dissolve the line between stage and water. The Vegas show to see if you see only one, book premium centre seats well ahead.

items.name: 'Michael Jackson ONE' by Cirque du Soleil
items.description: A high-energy acrobatic tribute at Mandalay Bay driven by MJ's biggest hits in state-of-the-art surround sound, the most family-friendly and instantly recognisable of the Cirque residencies. A crowd-pleaser across generations and languages.

items.name: 'KA' by Cirque du Soleil
items.description: A gravity-defying martial-arts epic at the MGM Grand built around a colossal rotating stage that flips to vertical mid-battle, theatrical engineering as spectacle. Grand, cinematic and easy to follow for non-English speakers.

items.name: 'Mystère' by Cirque du Soleil
items.description: The original Vegas Cirque show at Treasure Island, running since 1993, pure acrobatics, Taiko drums and surreal whimsy with a cast of 67, and no adult themes, so ideal for a family matinee. The most timeless entry point to the Cirque canon.

items.name: 'Mad Apple' by Cirque du Soleil
items.description: A New-York-themed cocktail of acrobatics, comedy, magic and a working stage bar at New York-New York, looser and more adult than the classics. Good for a night out with grown children rather than the whole family.

items.name: The Forum Shops at Caesars Palace
items.description: The original faux-Roman luxury mall, a painted sky that shifts dawn-to-dusk, animatronic fountains, and a flagship roll-call from Louis Vuitton and Gucci to Versace under one vaulted roof. The concierge can arrange after-hours private shopping and personal styling for high-spend guests.

items.name: The Shops at Crystals
items.description: The Strip's most rarefied retail, a Daniel Libeskind glass-and-steel canyon housing the largest concentration of ultra-luxury flagships in the US, from Louis Vuitton's island maison to Hermes, Bottega and Fendi. Discreet, uncrowded and built for serious shopping.

items.name: Wynn & Encore, Gardens, Atrium & Le Reve grounds
items.description: Steve Wynn's twin resorts trade neon for floral extravagance, carousels of parasols, a mountain and lake hidden behind the casino, and the Strip's most polished spa and boutique corridor. The quiet-luxury alternative for guests who want opulence without the theme-park energy.

items.name: Bellagio Gallery of Fine Art
items.description: A serious rotating exhibition space inside the Bellagio, recent shows have partnered with the Brooklyn Museum and major collections, a genuine cultural pause amid the slots. Small, curated and easily paired with the Conservatory next door.

items.name: High Roller Observation Wheel at The LINQ
items.description: At 550 feet the tallest observation wheel in North America, its 28 climate-controlled cabins making a 30-minute rotation over the whole Strip. Charter a private cabin with an in-cabin bar for sunset, a serene, safe, all-ages high above the chaos.

items.name: The STRAT SkyPod & Big Shot
items.description: The tallest freestanding observation tower in the US at 1,149 feet, with indoor and open-air decks, and, for the brave, the Big Shot ride that flings you to 1,081 feet with the city dangling beneath your feet. Ride-averse elders can stay on the deck while teens take the thrill rides.

items.name: AREA15, Meow Wolf's Omega Mart
items.description: A surreal, choose-your-own-adventure art experience disguised as a supermarket, where the freezer aisle is a secret portal into psychedelic worlds, 90 minutes to three hours of imaginative, all-ages exploration. The whole AREA15 district around it is Vegas's most creative corner, minutes from the Strip with free parking.

items.name: Fremont Street Experience
items.description: Old Vegas under a five-block LED canopy, Viva Vision light shows overhead, zip-liners flying past, and vintage neon that predates the mega-resorts. Grittier and more authentic than the Strip; go with a guide for the story behind the signs.

items.name: The Neon Museum & Neon Boneyard
items.description: An outdoor graveyard of more than 200 salvaged casino signs, the Stardust, the Moulin Rouge, the old Sahara, best seen on a guided night tour when select signs are re-lit. A photographer's dream and the truest window into the city's design history.

items.name: The Mob Museum
credentials: National Register of Historic Places, former Las Vegas Post Office and Courthouse (1933)
items.description: The National Museum of Organized Crime and Law Enforcement, set in the 1933 former federal courthouse where real Kefauver mob hearings were held, a genuinely gripping, artifact-rich account of how the mafia built and lost Las Vegas. A speakeasy and distillery hide in the basement.

items.name: The Grand Canyon, West Rim & Skywalk
items.description: The closest rim to Vegas at roughly 2.5 hours, on Hualapai tribal land, where the horseshoe-shaped Skywalk juts 70 feet out over a 4,000-foot drop to the Colorado. The classic Vegas day-trip, best done by private helicopter or SUV with a guide, and note phones must be locked away on the glass bridge itself.

items.name: The Grand Canyon, South Rim (National Park)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Grand Canyon National Park (1979)
items.description: The postcard canyon, endless layered vistas inside Grand Canyon National Park, about 4.5 hours' drive or a short scenic flight from Vegas, deserving of a full day or an overnight at El Tovar. Fly in by fixed-wing or helicopter to make it comfortable for elders and children.

items.name: Grand Canyon Helicopter Tour (with canyon-floor landing)
items.description: The definitive splurge, lift off from Vegas, cross Lake Mead and the Hoover Dam, then descend 4,000 feet to land on the canyon floor for a Champagne picnic by the Colorado. Private charters can be arranged with vegetarian catering and door-to-door hotel pickup.

items.name: Hoover Dam
credentials: National Historic Landmark (1985); American Society of Civil Engineers 'Historic Civil Engineering Landmark'
items.description: A 726-foot Art Deco engineering marvel just 40 minutes southeast of the Strip, spanning the Colorado at the Nevada-Arizona line, with a dam-interior tour and the sweeping Mike O'Callaghan-Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge above. An easy half-day, often folded into a Grand Canyon flight.

items.name: Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area
items.description: A 13-mile scenic loop through fiery sandstone escarpments just 20 minutes west of the Strip, the quickest escape into raw desert, good for a dawn drive, easy walks or serious rock-climbing. Close enough for a morning out before an afternoon by the pool.

items.name: Valley of Fire State Park
items.description: Nevada's oldest state park, under an hour northeast, flame-red Aztec sandstone, 3,000-year-old petroglyphs, and the Fire Wave's candy-striped rock that photographs like nowhere on Earth. Uncrowded and cinematic; pair it with the drive up to Zion.

items.name: Death Valley National Park
credentials: UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, Mojave and Colorado Deserts (includes Death Valley)
items.description: The lowest, hottest, driest place in North America, Badwater Basin's salt flats, Zabriskie Point's sculpted badlands and Mesquite dunes, about two hours west, a genuinely otherworldly full-day expedition. Go with a guide and travel in cooler months; summer heat is extreme.

items.name: Zion National Park
credentials: Zion is NOT a UNESCO site, do not add
items.description: Utah's soaring red-and-cream canyon of Navajo sandstone, about 2.5 hours from Vegas, a shuttle up the Virgin River gorge past cathedral cliffs, and the famous Narrows and Angels Landing for the fit. Doable as a very long day, but a night in Springdale rewards a UHNI itinerary.

items.name: Bryce Canyon National Park
credentials: Zion & Bryce are NOT UNESCO sites, do not add
items.description: An amphitheatre of thousands of orange hoodoo spires glowing at sunrise, about 4 hours from Vegas, usually combined with Zion into an overnight loop. High-altitude, cool and utterly unlike the desert below; a stargazing dark-sky reserve after dusk.

items.name: Antelope Canyon & Horseshoe Bend
items.description: The world's most photographed slot canyon, light beams slicing down between wave-carved Navajo sandstone walls near Page, Arizona, paired with the emerald Colorado horseshoe of the bend. A 4.5-hour drive each way, so best flown or built into a multi-day loop; access is guided-only on Navajo land.

items.name: Lake Powell
items.description: A vast turquoise reservoir threading through 96 slot-canyon fingers of red rock on the Utah-Arizona line, near Page, private houseboats and speedboats reach Rainbow Bridge and hidden coves. Pairs naturally with Antelope Canyon; a standout for families chartering their own vessel.

items.name: Sunset Strip Helicopter Flight
items.description: A 12-15 minute night flight low over the neon canyon, Bellagio's fountains, the Sphere and the Stratosphere lit beneath you, the single most romantic thing to do in the city. Private charters with Champagne and hotel transfers make it effortless.

items.name: Restaurant Guy Savoy at Caesars Palace
credentials: Michelin (Guy Savoy Paris holds 3 stars); the Las Vegas outpost is celebrated but the city has no active Michelin Guide
items.description: The Parisian three-Michelin-star maestro's only US outpost, artichoke-and-black-truffle soup, a Champagne-and-caviar room, and Strip-view windows above the fountains. Vegas's most serious fine-dining temple; the kitchen accommodates vegetarian tasting menus on request.

items.name: é by José Andrés
items.description: A hidden nine-seat counter behind the Bazaar at the Cosmopolitan, an avant-garde tasting-menu experience of spherified olives and edible illusions, among the hardest reservations in America. An intimate, theatrical splurge; flag dietary needs when the rare seat opens.

items.name: Joel Robuchon at MGM Grand
items.description: The late 'Chef of the Century's' opulent mansion-style dining room, a hushed jewel box of a menu that has long defined the top of the Vegas table. Ceremonial French service and a legendary bread cart; vegetarian menus available with notice.

items.name: Bavette's / Carbone / celebrity-chef steakhouse scene
items.description: Vegas is the world's densest cluster of celebrity-chef steakhouses and dining rooms, Carbone's red-sauce theatre, Bavette's supper-club glamour, Gordon Ramsay's and Nobu's flagships all within a few blocks. The concierge can secure the impossible tables and a private room for a family celebration.

items.name: Rutba Indian Kitchen
items.description: A polished Indian dining room right on the Strip built for exactly this traveller, clearly marked vegetarian, vegan and Jain options in a menu that ranges North to South. A reassuring anchor for guests who want familiar, well-executed Indian food between the spectacles.

items.name: Divine Dosa & Biryani
items.description: Regional, North and South Indian cooking a short walk from the Wynn, crisp dosas, biryanis and a broad pure-vegetarian selection that satisfies homesick and Jain-conscious palates alike. A dependable, unfussy table close to the action.

items.name: Marquee / XS / Encore Beach Club, Dayclub & Pool Scene
items.description: Vegas invented the dayclub, daybed pools with world-headline DJs, cabanas that become open-air suites, and a see-and-be-seen energy unmatched anywhere. For UHNI guests, a private cabana or bungalow with bottle service and a host turns the crush into a curated day.

items.name: The Chandelier Bar at The Cosmopolitan
items.description: A three-storey bar suspended inside a two-million-crystal chandelier, the Strip's most photogenic cocktail perch, with a secret 'PsychoCandy' menu on the upper level. A stylish, low-key nightcap that doesn't require a club reservation.

items.name: Fountains-view fine dining, Le Cirque & Prime at Bellagio
items.description: Lakeside tables timed to the fountains erupting outside the window, Le Cirque's jewel-box French room and Prime's steakhouse both frame the water ballet as dinner theatre. Ask the concierge to reserve the front tables for the show and to note any Jain or vegetarian needs.

items.name: Caesars Palace, Roman grandeur & the Garden of the Gods pools
items.description: The resort that set the template, marble colonnades, replica statuary, and a seven-pool Roman bathing complex that is a destination in itself. Beyond the Forum Shops, the property rewards a slow wander; villa suites and Qua Baths anchor a discreet high-roller stay.

items.name: Mount Charleston & Spring Mountains
items.description: A pine-forested alpine escape rising to nearly 12,000 feet just 45 minutes northwest, 30 degrees cooler than the valley, with hiking, a historic lodge and winter snow. The locals' hidden antidote to the desert heat, and a serene half-day for families.

items.name: Lake Mead National Recreation Area
items.description: The Hoover Dam's vast reservoir, America's largest by capacity, where private boats, kayaks and scenic drives open up hidden coves 40 minutes from the Strip. Charter a boat with a captain for a calm morning on the water before the day heats up.

items.name: Seven Magic Mountains
items.description: Ugo Rondinone's seven towers of fluorescent boulders stacked against raw desert, 20 minutes south of the Strip off I-15, a free, endlessly Instagrammable land-art installation. A quick, striking stop en route in or out of the city.

items.name: Joël Robuchon
items.description: The late 'Chef of the Century's' jewel-box mansion, the most decorated fine-dining room in the city, twenty years on.

items.name: Restaurant Guy Savoy
items.description: The three-Michelin-star Paris master's only US restaurant, his artichoke-and-truffle soup, overlooking the Strip.

items.name: Le Cirque
items.description: The Maccioni family's silk-tented circus over the Bellagio lake, old-world French service and a view of the fountains.

items.name: Wing Lei
items.description: The only Forbes Five-Star Chinese restaurant in North America, imperial Cantonese, and a tableside Peking duck.

items.name: é by José Andrés
credentials: James Beard Foundation, José Andrés, Outstanding Chef & Humanitarian of the Year
items.description: An eight-seat counter hidden inside Jaleo, Spanish avant-garde theatre from the mind that helped shape elBulli.

items.name: Bazaar Meat by José Andrés
items.area: The Palazzo at The Venetian, The Strip
credentials: James Beard Foundation, José Andrés, Outstanding Chef
items.description: José Andrés's carnivore's theatre, reborn in 2025 in a vast new Palazzo room, whole roasts, caviar cones and fire.

items.name: Carbone
items.description: Major Food Group's Italian-American time-machine, captains in dinner jackets, spicy rigatoni vodka and pure swagger.

items.name: CUT by Wolfgang Puck
items.area: The Palazzo at The Venetian, The Strip
items.description: Wolfgang Puck's modern steakhouse, dry-aged American and Japanese wagyu in a sleek, high-energy room.

items.name: Michael Mina
credentials: James Beard Foundation, Michael Mina, Best Chef Pacific
items.description: The James Beard-winning chef's flagship, seafood-led modern American in a soaring Bellagio room.

items.name: Mizumi
items.description: Wynn's Japanese room built around a private garden and waterfall, teppanyaki, sushi and robata in serene surrounds.

items.name: SW Steakhouse
items.description: Wynn's signature steakhouse on the Lake of Dreams, prime beef and a nightly light-and-water show at the window.

items.name: Sinatra
items.description: A love letter to Ol' Blue Eyes, regional Italian classics amid the singer's Oscar and memorabilia.

items.name: L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon
items.description: Robuchon's red-and-black counter beside his mansion, the same legendary kitchen, at the pass, à la carte.

items.name: Kusa Nori
items.description: A refined, contemporary Japanese room that quietly earned a Forbes Four-Star, sushi and kaiseki-style precision.

items.name: Delilah
credentials: The World's 50 Best Restaurants, 50 Best Discovery
items.description: A modern-day supper club inside Wynn's Tower Suites, 1940s glamour, live music and tableside luxury classics.

items.name: Jean Georges Steakhouse
credentials: Pedigree: Jean-Georges Vongerichten, multiple Michelin stars (New York)
items.description: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's refined steakhouse, his signatures and a prime-beef programme in a sleek ARIA room.

items.name: Spago by Wolfgang Puck
credentials: Pedigree: Wolfgang Puck, James Beard Outstanding Chef & Restaurateur
items.description: The restaurant that started celebrity-chef Las Vegas, Wolfgang Puck's Californian flagship, now on the Bellagio lake.

items.name: Bardot Brasserie
credentials: James Beard Foundation, Michael Mina pedigree
items.description: Michael Mina's Belle Époque Parisian brasserie, onion soup, escargot and one of the best weekend brunches on the Strip.

items.name: Costa di Mare
items.description: Wynn's Italian coastal room, whole Mediterranean fish flown in daily, beside a private lagoon terrace.

items.name: The Chandelier Bar
credentials: A signature Las Vegas landmark bar (The Cosmopolitan)
items.description: A three-storey bar built inside a two-million-crystal chandelier, the most photographed drink in Las Vegas.

items.name: Parasol Down / Parasol Up
credentials: Signature bars of the Forbes 5-Star Wynn Las Vegas
items.description: Wynn's whimsical twin bars under floating parasols, Parasol Down overlooks the Lake of Dreams show.

items.name: Electra Cocktail Club
credentials: A signature cocktail bar of The Venetian Resort
items.description: A shimmering, high-energy cocktail bar wrapped in a wall of colour-shifting video, serious drinks, glossy room.

items.name: Apex Social Club
credentials: Among the highest rooftop bars in Las Vegas
items.description: A 55th-floor rooftop lounge with a wrap-around Strip view, one of the best skyline vantages in the city.

items.name: XS Nightclub
credentials: Consistently ranked the top-grossing US nightclub (industry revenue rankings)
items.description: For years the highest-grossing nightclub in America, a gold-drenched megaclub opening onto the Encore pool.

items.name: Omnia
credentials: One of the highest-grossing US nightclubs (industry revenue rankings)
items.description: Caesars' three-storey spectacle, crowned by a vast kinetic chandelier that descends over the main room.

items.name: Hakkasan
credentials: One of the highest-grossing US nightclubs (industry revenue rankings)
items.description: A five-storey nightlife-and-dining colossus, Cantonese fine dining below, a stadium of a nightclub above.

items.name: Marquee
credentials: Consistently ranked among the top US nightclubs by revenue
items.description: The Cosmopolitan's indoor-outdoor giant, a dome, a terrace over the Strip and a dayclub that runs into the night.

plan.heading: 3 days in Las Vegas, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Arrive and settle into a suite at the Waldorf Astoria's quiet tower above the noise.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Bellagio's Gallery of Fine Art and a slow look at the conservatory.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Joël Robuchon at the MGM Grand, the full menu.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: An early drive to Red Rock Canyon before the heat, the scenic loop with a guide.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Return for the spa and the pool through the afternoon.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A show, a residency or Cirque, then a late table at Estiatorio Milos.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A private helicopter to the Grand Canyon's West Rim, landing on the floor for a quiet moment.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Back by early afternoon, lunch at Wing Lei, the city's Michelin Cantonese table.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Cocktails high over the Strip, then the flight out or a last dinner at Carbone.

neighbourhoods.heading: Where to base yourself
neighbourhoods.pairWith: Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York

items.name: The Strip (Bellagio / Wynn end)
items.description: The central artery of resorts, shows and dining, convenient and spectacular, if relentless.

items.name: Downtown / Fremont
items.description: Older, grittier Vegas with vintage neon and a livelier local scene, for travellers who want character over polish.

items.name: Summerlin
items.description: Quiet master-planned suburb against Red Rock, with resort golf, a calm base away from the noise.

events.name: Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix
events.note: The night race runs a street circuit down the Strip past Caesars and the Sphere; book far ahead as the city fills.

events.name: Wrangler National Finals Rodeo
events.note: Ten days of championship rodeo at the Thomas & Mack Center that transform the city's mood.

events.name: New Year's Eve on the Strip
events.note: Fireworks launch from the resort rooftops in one of the largest street celebrations in the country.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Suite guests at Wynn, Bellagio or the Aria Sky suites get a dedicated host who arranges tables, shows and dining, use them; the ESTA is required in advance, and July desert heat is extreme, so plan outdoor time for early morning or evening.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Harry Reid International (LAS), minutes from the Strip; the finest resorts send a private car or limousine, and true VIPs use the private-jet terminal at Henderson.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A house car or resort limousine handles the Strip; walking works within a resort complex but distances between properties are deceptively long, so ride.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: US eSIM is flawless and resort Wi-Fi is fast; connectivity is never a concern here.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: US dollar; cards everywhere, but keep cash for casino tables and tips; tip dealers, valets and hosts generously, it is the currency of good service here.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: March-May and October-November are the pleasant windows, warm and dry; avoid the desert furnace of June-August when daytime heat is punishing, and the cold desert nights of December-January.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No nonstop from India; routings run via a Gulf hub or a US gateway (Emirates via Dubai, or Air India via San Francisco then a short domestic hop), roughly 19-22 hours door to door in J or F. Fly into San Francisco or Los Angeles in J, then a private or first-class domestic leg into Las Vegas.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations beyond routine; ESTA or US visa required in advance. The Strip and resorts are safe and heavily managed; the desert heat is the real risk, so hydrate and limit midday exposure in summer. Tap water is safe but bottled is common.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian is easy across the resort restaurants and Jain is manageable in the Indian venues; the city has a solid Indian dining scene. Consider Saffron or the Indian tables on and off the Strip for dependable vegetarian and Jain options.
